changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: HospitalService.code: a stable business key so the system can look a catalogue entry up by meaning instead of by display name. Needed because the consultation bill line item has to be priced from "the general consultation" entry, and matching on name/serviceType is fragile (someone renames the service and billing silently breaks). Nullable so rows that predate this column keep working; unique when present.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: BillLineItem.source_ref: links a charge back to the thing that generated it, formatted as sourceType colon entityId, for example CONSULTATION:42 or LAB:17. Without this, incremental charging is not idempotent (a retried "complete consultation" double-charges) and there is no way to void one charge. The unique index is on (bill_id, source_ref) and is safe with NULLs: Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so any number of hand-entered lines can coexist.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: Optimistic locking (@Version) on the four entities whose state is mutated by concurrent clinical events: two nurses prescribing the same drug (stock reservation), a lab result landing while a prescription is dispensed (visit status recompute), and a payment confirmation racing a bill total rewrite.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment:
Lookup indexes.
audit_log: every correction lookup is "history for this entity", which is currently a sequential scan.
patient.identity_document_number is indexed for the exact-match duplicate check but is DELIBERATELY NOT UNIQUE. phase1.md requires that when an exact ID match is found, Reception may still "confirm creating a new one anyway" — a unique constraint would make that documented override impossible to perform.
